article.title: Russian strike kills at least 33 in eastern Ukraine in deadliest single attack this year - Egypt Independent
article.description: Kyiv, Ukraine — At least 33 people were killed on Thursday when a Russian strike caused two public buses to catch fire in eastern Ukraine, local authorities said, making it the deadliest single attack this year.
paragraphs: Search for Egypt World Middle East Business Science Culture Life & Style Opinion Facebook X RSS Search for World Russian strike kills at least 33 in eastern Ukraine in deadliest single attack this year By Kosta Gak, Sophie Tanno CNN October 11, 2026 Facebook X LinkedIn Kyiv, Ukraine — At least 33 people were killed on Thursday when a Russian strike caused two public buses to catch fire in eastern Ukraine , local authorities said, making it the deadliest single attack this year. Another 18 people were injured in the attack in Kramatorsk , a city in the Donetsk region, which prompted authorities there to shut down the public transport system and urge people to move to safer parts of the country.

“The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians,” said Vadym Filashkin, the head of the Donetsk regional military administration. “For them, a bus full of passengers is an attractive target precisely because a single strike can kill as many people as possible.”
The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SES) said the Russian strike caused a fire on two buses and in the surrounding area.

Police in Donetsk said Russian drones targeted officers who were helping victims of the strike. Police were still working to identify the victims of the strike, with some bodies having to be pieced together from fragments, they said in a statement.

Footage they released of the rescue operation shows bodies strewn across the road. Drones can be seen near the scene of the strike as responders load the injured onto stretchers and into emergency vehicles.

article.title: Strikes hit Yemen
article.description: ADEN, Yemen, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group struck the international airport in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden on Friday...
paragraphs: ADEN, Yemen, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group struck the international airport in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden on Friday night, Aden's security administration said, while the Saudi-led coalition said earlier it had intercepted fresh drones and missiles over Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea.
Aden's security administration said in a statement that two missiles landed inside the grounds of Aden International Airport, with preliminary information indicating no casualties.

A local security official earlier told Xinhua that two missiles had landed near Aden International Airport, while a third struck a military base near the headquarters of the Saudi-led coalition forces in Al Buraiqa district in western Aden.

Three powerful explosions rocked the city, the temporary seat of the internationally recognized Yemeni government, during the attack, a Xinhua reporter on the ground and local residents said. Ambulances were seen heading toward the affected areas.

Shortly after the attack, Houthi-run al-Masirah TV cited a military leader within the group as saying the group had targeted "the headquarters of Saudi forces and weapons depots" at Badr military camp near Aden International Airport.

article.title: Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks
article.description: TEHRAN — Iran on Friday denied having anything to do with attacks by Yemen
paragraphs: Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.

A Saudi-led military coalition has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government for more than a decade, and reported on Friday having intercepted more missiles and drones as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from the Houthis.
A day earlier, a Saudi foreign ministry official said Iran had "encouraged" the escalation, which Tehran denied.
"The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations," Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement.

article.description: Oct 17 (Reuters) - Missiles struck Yemen’s Aden International Airport on Friday, while a Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile headed f… Leggi
paragraphs: Oct 17 (Reuters) - Missiles struck Yemen’s Aden International Airport on Friday, while a Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile headed for the Red Sea city of Yanbu, a key Saudi oil hub that allows exports to avoid the Strait of Hormuz.
The coalition said it had also destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones in Saudi Arabia’s Southern and Riyadh regions. It did not identify the attackers.

In Aden in southern Yemen, two missiles landed on the airport grounds, the Aden Security Department said, blaming the Iran-aligned Houthi group. It said the incident was the second attack on the facility in less than a week. The Houthis did not immediately claim responsibility.
No casualties were reported. A Yemenia Airways flight bound for Cairo was preparing for takeoff when the missiles landed, the security department said.

Yanbu is a key outlet for Saudi oil exports, allowing the kingdom to ship crude to international markets via the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The vital waterway has been largely throttled by Iran since the US and Israel launched attacks on the country in February.

Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 16 (ANI): Air India has extended the cancellation of all its flights to and from Riyadh , Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, 2026, citing the evolving security situation in Saudi Arabia amid recent attacks on civilian airports and aviation infrastructure in the Kingdom. The development comes as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Council strongly condemned the attacks on civilian airports, aircraft and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, expressing solidarity with the country's government and people. In a statement posted on X, Air India said it was closely monitoring developments and assessing the situation to determine when operations could safely resume. “In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, all Air India flights to and from Riyadh , Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until 20 October 2026. We are closely monitoring developments and continuously assessing the situation to ensure the safe resumption of operations,” the airline said. The carrier added that passengers affected by the cancellations were being offered a full refund, reiterating that the safety and security of passengers and crew remained its highest priority. The ICAO Council, in a statement issued on Thursday, condemned the recent attacks in the strongest terms and conveyed its deepest sympathies and condolences to the victims and their families. The condemnation followed a statement delivered by Saudi Arabia before the ICAO Council on October 8. According to the aviation body's statement, the Council deplored the targeting of civil aviation infrastructure and the resulting impact on aviation operations, as well as the threat such attacks posed to aviation safety and security and international peace and security. The latest extension by Air India follows earlier flight suspensions announced by Indian carriers IndiGo and Akasa Air amid escalating security concerns in the Middle East. IndiGo had announced cancellations of flights to and from Riyadh , Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 17, advising passengers to check their flight status before leaving for the airport. The airline said it was coordinating with relevant authorities and providing updates to passengers through the contact details supplied at the time of booking. Akasa Air had also extended the suspension of flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 17, citing the escalating security situation and associated risks to safe flight operations. In its advisory, Akasa Air said affected passengers could opt for a full refund or reschedule their travel without additional charges. The flight disruptions come amid reports of attacks on Saudi aviation infrastructure and heightened security concerns affecting air travel in the region. The death toll from the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh rose to 13 after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed the death of an Indian national who had been injured in the incident. Amid the military escalation, the Houthis issued a broad warning to international airlines, foreign workers and commercial travellers to avoid Saudi aviation hubs, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe, with an explicit exception for the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Air India said it would continue monitoring the situation and assess developments before resuming operations, while the ICAO Council's condemnation underscored international concern over attacks targeting civilian aviation infrastructure. The International Civil Aviation Organization is a United Nations specialised agency that brings together 193 member states to develop global standards and recommended practices for safe, secure and sustainable international civil aviation. (ANI)
